findings.F1: When a coin's 24-hour volatility is at or above its 720-hour average, its next 24 hours run against its prior 24-hour move once that move is at least one usual 24-hour move. Unusual move: +70 bps (t 5.9, 1917 cases) for moves of 1 to 2 usual moves, +61 bps (t 2.5, 687) for 2 to 3, and +149 bps (t 3.1, 328) beyond 3. On the grid shifted by 12 hours the same 1-to-2 bucket gives +46 bps (t 3.4, 1811 cases). Per case this is 2 to 7 times the 0.19 % cost of a buy and a sell.
findings.F2: In low volatility the same 24-hour reversal is absent or reversed. For 1 to 2 usual moves it is +13 bps (t 0.9, 1202 cases) on one grid and −35 bps (t −2.6, 1135) on the shifted grid, so the reversal belongs to the high-volatility regime.
findings.F3: The 24-hour reversal after a 24-hour move of at least one usual move shows up separately in each of the 6 coins on the window-start grid, from +25 bps (BTC, t 1.9) to +83 bps (ZEC, t 3.0). It holds in both halves of the windows: +65 bps (t 6.3, 2049 cases) in the early half and +50 bps (t 3.5, 2152) in the late half.
findings.F4: The reversal is stronger after falls than after rises. After a 24-hour fall of at least one usual move the next 24 hours rise +82 bps more than usual (t 6.0, 2011 cases); after a rise they fall +34 bps more than usual (t 3.0, 2190). On the shifted grid the figures are +43 bps (t 3.0) after falls and −9 bps (t −0.7) after rises.
findings.F5: The tested 2-hour overreaction keeps reverting well past its 8-hour horizon. In high volatility, 2-hour moves of 3 to 4 usual moves give +38 bps over 8 hours (t 1.9, 579 cases) but +165 bps over 24 hours (t 3.0, 195 cases, strength 0.32). Moves beyond 4 give +57 bps over 8 hours (t 2.4) and +162 bps over 24 hours (t 2.3). Over 8 hours, only 2-hour moves above 2 usual moves (+28 to +57 bps) cover the 19 bps cost.
findings.F6: Most of the 8-hour cases are too small to pay. High-volatility 2-hour moves under one usual move make up 11188 of about 18200 cases and carry +3.7 bps (t 1.3), against a cost of 19 bps.
findings.F7: Over 72 hours there is no reversal of a 72-hour move; if anything it continues. Moves beyond 2 usual moves give −113 bps (t −1.8, 350 cases), so the reversal is a 1-day effect.
findings.F8: The book loses on the positions it holds long, not on its short ones. Trades held 8 hours or less net +0.61 % each (24937 trades). Trades held 16 to 48 hours net −1.92 % (9408 trades) and those beyond 48 hours net −5.05 % (2056 trades), for an overall net of −0.36 % per trade.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour volatility is high against its own past month, its 24-hour return is followed by a move the opposite way over the next 24 hours. The larger its 24-hour return against its usual 24-hour move, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: A day-long overreaction in a volatile coin can be faded with a move per case several times the cost of a round trip, unlike the 8-hour version.
ideas.name: volatile daily move reverses

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour fall is followed by a rise over the next 24 hours, and the deeper the fall against its usual 24-hour move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: Buying after a sharp one-day fall captures the strongest side of the daily reversal, which a trader can take without shorting.
ideas.name: daily fall rebounds next day

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour volatility is high, its large 2-hour move is followed by a move the opposite way over the next 24 hours. The larger the 2-hour move against its usual 2-hour move, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: The tested overreaction is worth more held for a day than for 8 hours, so fewer, longer bets on the largest moves can clear the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: two-hour overreaction reverses daylong
